en-US.title: Venture: History Nearby
en-US.subtitle: The history of where you stand
en-US.promoText: The vanished palace, the two-century prison, the plaque you've never read — every story within a walk of you, told in about a minute.
en-US.description:
A nuclear reactor ran in Greenwich until 1996. Nobody walking past would ever know.

Venture is a history app for the ground under your feet. Open it anywhere and it finds what happened around you — the palace that burned, the prison that stood two hundred years, the plaque you've passed a hundred times and never read. Each one told in about a minute. Then, if you like, it walks you there.

WHAT'S AROUND YOU

Everything within a walk, nearest first, each with a photograph so you'll know it when you see it and one line on why it's worth the detour.

Some of it still stands. Some of it is a car park now. A palace that burned down four centuries ago still has a location, and Venture will still take you to the spot.

A STORY, NOT A PLAQUE

Every place gets a proper telling: the surprising thing first, the dates afterwards. Read it, or put the phone in your pocket and let it talk while you walk.

Whole neighborhoods get the longer treatment — a story in chapters, a timeline you can jump around inside, and every other tale standing on the same ground.

THE WALK THERE

A compass with a bearing and a distance, for when that's all you need. Turn-by-turn directions for when it isn't. Both work perfectly well for places that aren't there any more.

WHAT YOU KEEP

Save anything worth returning to and take it with you — saved stories open with no signal at all, underground or overseas.

Venture quietly notes what you've read and where you've stood, so coming back to an area shows you what you haven't seen yet.

FROM AN ARMCHAIR

You don't have to be there. Search a town before you visit, or the street you grew up on, and read it from the sofa.

Coverage is richest in Britain and thins the further out you go.

No account. No advertising. Nothing following you around. Your location stays on your phone, where it sorts what's nearby and points the compass, and it goes nowhere else.
